messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing weird double-charging on streaming when clients disconnect + reconnect? User reports charged for 'partial tokens' twice (before and after reconnect).
kevin: Haven't seen it in prod alerts but we've had a couple billing tickets. Do you have a repro or logs?
maria: Pasting a trimmed trace from their session:
```
CONNECT id=abc123 key=org_42 stream_id=xyz
EMIT tokens=14
DISCONNECT reason=network
RECONNECT resume_id=abc123 stream_id=xyz
EMIT tokens=8  # client resumed and server re-sent prefix
CLOSE
```
End result: charged for 22 tokens but user says they only received 14 unique tokens. Looks like the resume path re-emitted prefix tokens and we accounted both emissions.
aj: That matches a race we've discussed — we currently increment counters on every EMIT event. On reconnect the resume path emits prefix slices and we don't dedupe by resume_id.
sophie: Is the accounting keyed to api_key or org? This matters for fairness across shared org keys.
maria: This was per-key. Customer uses a single org-key shared across devices, they expect per-client fairness but enterprise billing expects per-org pooling.
kevin: Two axes here: correctness (no double-billing for the same logical output) and abuse/fairness (prevent one connection from gaming burst credits).
aj: Proposal: introduce a short reservation window on connection + an idempotent resume_id. Flow: on first connect create a reservation record: reserve N tokens (small default, e.g., 32) with TTL 30s; emit counts against reservation; on close/expiry reconcile actual usage and commit or reclaim remainder. On reconnect with same resume_id, attach to existing reservation and avoid recounting already-accounted prefix tokens.
maria: That sounds promising. How do we handle clients that open multiple simultaneous connections with same key (multi-device)?
sophie: For per-org quotas we can allow pooling (reservations draw from org pool). For per-key quotas the reservation should be per-connection/resume_id; but we should also cap per-key concurrent reservation count to prevent sprawl.
kevin: Implementation details: we need a single source of truth for reservation state (fast kv, e.g., redis) with ops TTL and compare-and-set for commit. Also need resume_id carried by client and validated.
aj: Example header we can add: `X-Resume-Id: <uuid>` and server will return `X-Reservation-Id` and `X-Reservation-ttl`. If resume_id matches an existing reservation we'll attach.
maria: How do we dedupe prefix tokens? The runtime emits tokens by chunk; when resuming it may re-emit overlapping tokens for safety. We need token-level dedupe or a simpler approach: mark all tokens emitted before disconnect as 'committed' and ignore identical offsets when resume claims same offset via resume_id.
aj: Token-level dedupe is heavy. Better to treat the resume path as continuing an existing reservation: don't create a new reservation atomically, so duplicated EMITs only decrement the reservation balance but don't create new charges. We only charge (increment billing counters) on commit. But we currently bill on EMIT to simplify realtime billing.
kevin: Moving to commit-time billing changes a lot. Alternative: keep realtime billing but write a short-lived 'claimed offsets' set per resume_id, and when EMIT arrives check if offset already claimed. That requires clients to send offsets or seq numbers. Can we get clients to send `X-Stream-Seq: <n>`?
sophie: Many clients already have seq behavior (SSE/ws). We could require seq only if resume header present. Backward compatible default: if no resume requested, current behavior unchanged.
maria: Telemetry: we need metrics to understand impact. Suggest these new metrics: `streaming.reservations.created`, `streaming.reservations.reclaimed`, `streaming.partialtokens.duplicated`, `streaming.resume.attachments`, and a gauge `streaming.inflight_reservations`.
aj: Also add tracing tags: resume_id, reservation_id, org_id, key_id so we can pivot in the console.
kevin: UX in console: show pending reservations per org on the quota dashboard, and an admin toggle for `stream_reserve_window` per deployment for safe canary.
maria: Rollout plan idea: default disabled. Canary on 5% of traffic (feature flag per org). Monitor `partialtokens.duplicated` and billing deltas for two weeks, then shrink TTL and expand.
opsbot: quota-bot: detected spike: streaming.partialtokens.duplicated +120% over baseline in last 6h for org_42.
maria: That's the customer. We'll flip them to the canary and test.
sophie: Edge cases: reconciling across regions — if client reconnects to a different region we need global reservation lookup (consistent redis or central control plane). That adds latency; maybe use a global lease stored in central control plane with local cache.
aj: Also consider failure modes: if we reserve but control-plane loses lease before commit, we should have reclaim logic and maybe a safety window where we don't bill until commit.
kevin: Action items:
- kevin: draft API/headers RFC (X-Resume-Id + seq semantics) and spec how billing ties to reservation (ETA end of day).
- aj: prototype reservation store + Redis CAS and metrics (ETA 3 days).
- maria: repro harness that simulates disconnect/reconnect/prefix replays + compare billing (ETA 2 days).
- sophie: update quota dashboard mockups to surface inflight reservations + reclaimed tokens (ETA 1 week).
- ops: evaluate billing implications for past invoices and refund automation (follow-up with finance).
maria: Any objections to the RFC approach?
kevin: No major objections. We should keep realtime billing for non-resume flows to avoid regressions. For resume flows we use reservation + seq dedupe.
aj: I'll throw together a PoC that adds `X-Reservation-Id` in response and honors `X-Resume-Id` on reconnect.
sophie: :thumbsup: make sure to include telemetry labels for org/key so we can alert.
maria: Thanks all. I'll file a ticket linking logs and add the affected customer. Reactions: :eyes: :thumbsup:
quota-bot: note: created ticket Q-1872 for reservation RFC tracking (assigned to kevin).
